algorithms.title: Reverse a List In Place
algorithms.summary: Swap elements from the outside inward.
algorithms.whenToUse: Reversing or comparing elements from both ends.
algorithms.code:
def reverse_items(items):
    left, right = 0, len(items) - 1
    while left < right:
        items[left], items[right] = items[right], items[left]
        left += 1
        right -= 1
    return items

print(reverse_items([1, 2, 3, 4]))  # [4, 3, 2, 1]

algorithms.title: Insertion Sort
algorithms.summary: Insert each value into the sorted portion before it.
algorithms.whenToUse: Learning sorting; nearly sorted small arrays.
algorithms.code:
def insertion_sort(nums):
    nums = nums.copy()
    for i in range(1, len(nums)):
        value = nums[i]
        j = i - 1
        while j >= 0 and nums[j] > value:
            nums[j + 1] = nums[j]
            j -= 1
        nums[j + 1] = value
    return nums

print(insertion_sort([5, 2, 4, 1]))  # [1, 2, 4, 5]

walkthrough: Treat the first element as sorted.

algorithms.complexityExplanation: Nested shifts can take quadratic time; this version copies input first.
commonMistakes: The copy uses O(n) memory; in-place insertion sort uses O(1).

algorithms.title: Generate Subsets (Backtracking)
algorithms.summary: Explore include/exclude choices and undo choices afterward.
algorithms.code:
def subsets(nums):
    result = []
    path = []
    def backtrack(index):
        if index == len(nums):
            result.append(path.copy())
            return
        backtrack(index + 1)
        path.append(nums[index])
        backtrack(index + 1)
        path.pop()
    backtrack(0)
    return result

print(subsets([1, 2]))  # [[], [2], [1], [1, 2]]

walkthrough: For each element, first explore excluding it.
Then include it and explore again.
algorithms.complexityExplanation: There are 2^n subsets; copying each can take O(n).
commonMistakes: Append path.copy(), not path; undo changes with pop().
